findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the recall claim: state explicitly that the COMMITTED token tier does NOT fire on the modal unlocked-twin corpus class (git rm/commit, getmtime+remove on index.lock) and that portable recall on that class is delivered by the noisy/project tier — OR add a committed trigger signal (e.g. a removed `with <lock>:`/transaction-wrapper scan, or a shared-store file glob) so the built-in catches the modal class; and align AC#2 so its committed-trigger unit test names which corpus hunks are covered by committed vs project tokens.
evidence: Plan Approach: 'a committed high-precision cross-stack token list ... plus a project-extensible noisy tier in .rebar/criteria_routing.json ... noisy tier measured +21%; it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here'
eclectic-spotted-barb root cause: '_prune_queue_events ... raw, unlocked, whole-index git rm + git commit' — no thread/async/lock token in the diff body
fine-wisteria-solenodon root cause: 'reads os.path.getmtime(lock_file), judges stale, then unconditionally os.remove(lock_file)' — no committed token present

AC#2: 'fires deterministically from diff content via the committed high-precision token trigger (added and removed lines) ... checked by unit tests over corpus-derived diff hunks' — the modal-class corpus hunks do not contain committed tokens
ABSENCE: the plan does not reconcile 'committed trigger fires on corpus-derived hunks' (AC#2) with 'the noisy (project) tier is what makes the corpus bugs trigger' (body)
findings.finding: The committed high-precision token trigger — the built-in overlay's guaranteed (project-config-independent) behavior — does not fire on ANY of the three unlocked-twin corpus races the plan names as this codebase's MODAL class. eclectic-spotted-barb (raw `git rm`+`git commit`), grassgreen-clotty-duck/malevolent-emigratory-umbrette (same class), and fine-wisteria-solenodon (`os.path.getmtime` then `os.remove` on index.lock) contain none of the thread/async/DB-lock/file-primitive tokens the committed tier scans for. The plan concedes recall on these depends on the project-extensible NOISY tier ('it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here'). So a fresh install of the built-in overlay in another project would miss its own modal filesystem/store race class — the primary problem the plan cites. This also creates an internal AC tension: AC#2 promises the overlay 'fires deterministically from diff content via the committed high-precision token trigger ... checked by unit tests over corpus-derived diff hunks', but the modal-class corpus hunks fire ONLY via project config, so the committed-trigger unit test can pass only on non-modal-class (fabricated) hunks.
findings.location: Approach section ('committed high-precision cross-stack token list ... plus a project-extensible noisy tier ... it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here'); Acceptance Criteria #1 and #2
scenarios: A different project installs the built-in concurrency overlay without adding its own trigger_tokens; its own git-index/lockfile unlocked-twin race is not escalated

The AC#2 committed-trigger unit test is written against a fabricated hunk containing e.g. `flock`/`Lock(` (passes) while the actual modal corpus hunks (git rm+commit, getmtime+remove) would not have fired the committed tier

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: Disambiguate 'trigger' (lexical fire) from 'caught/surfaced' (rubric finding) in the Approach and reconcile the four-bug accounting (which of the four fire lexically vs which produce a finding).
evidence: 'it is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here'
'Accepted v1 blind spots ... no-twin races (the greisen-draconian-annelid ... class) and CI-level CAS/backoff judgment (the fervid-boring-python class)'
A bug that fires the overlay lexically but that the rubric cannot judge is both 'triggering' and a 'blind spot' — the plan does not name this distinction
findings.finding: The plan asserts two accepted v1 blind spots (greisen-draconian-annelid no-twin, fervid-boring-python CI CAS) yet also states the noisy tier 'is what makes three of the four corpus bugs trigger here', without distinguishing lexical 'trigger' (overlay fires) from 'caught/surfaced' (rubric produces a finding). Four bugs minus two blind spots does not reconcile with three triggering unless 'trigger' and 'blind spot' operate on different layers, which is left implicit.
findings.location: Approach paragraph (blind-spots sentence vs noisy-tier sentence)
scenarios: A reader trying to map the four corpus bugs to trigger/catch outcomes cannot tell whether greisen triggers-but-misses or does not trigger at all
The eval author cannot tell whether greisen belongs in a 'fires but no finding' family or a 'no-fire' family
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause clarifying, e.g. 'three of the four fire lexically; greisen fires but the rubric cannot surface it (documented blind spot), fervid neither fires nor is judged.'

findings.checklist_item: State the eval gate's pass bar in the plan (e.g. required recall on the unlocked-twin recall family, max fire rate on the no-fire families, and the required outcome on the check-then-act hard-FP control).
evidence: 'checked by the standing eval rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency passing its gate'
'a standing eval spec distilled from the traced corpus (recall and no-fire families, including the deliberate check-then-act hard-FP control)'
Signal (2) implicit acceptance criteria: the numeric gate that makes the eval pass/fail is unstated
findings.finding: AC1 defers to 'the standing eval rebar prompt eval code-review-concurrency passing its gate' but the plan never states the gate's pass bar (recall threshold on the recall family, allowed fire rate on the no-fire families, or the hard-FP control's required outcome). The pass condition is an implicit acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC1; Child decomposition (eval spec child)
scenarios: An executor writes the eval spec but must invent the pass threshold, risking a gate that is trivially green or unattainably strict
Reviewer cannot confirm AC1 is met without knowing what 'passing its gate' means
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Approach or AC1 fixing the gate, e.g. 'the eval passes when it recalls all unlocked-twin recall cases, produces zero fires on the no-fire family, and does not fire on the check-then-act hard-FP control.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach, judge (and either adopt or defensibly reject with a stated reason) a committed shared-state-file GLOB trigger tier for the concurrency overlay (store/lock/drain paths) as a structurally-different alternative to token-only committed triggering, given that all three unlocked-twin corpus bugs live in such files and the overlay machinery already supports committed applies_to globs.
evidence: Plan: overlay ships with empty committed applies_to and relies on 'a committed high-precision cross-stack token list' for deterministic firing

Corpus file paths are shared-store sources: enrich_drain.py, _commands/fsck.py, purge_bridge.py — a committed applies_to glob over store/lock/drain paths would fire on the modal class from committed config
The machinery already unions committed applies_to globs (glob_triggered_overlays) alongside content triggers, so a glob tier is a small, structurally-distinct addition
ABSENCE: the plan states no rationale for token-only committed triggering over a shared-state file-glob tier
findings.finding: APPROACH SELECTION: the plan chooses a content(token)-triggered overlay but does not weigh a structurally-different GLOB-triggered tier keyed on shared-state file paths (e.g. **/_store/**, **/*lock*, **/enrich_drain*, drain/sidecar/prune sources). All three unlocked-twin corpus bugs live in such files (enrich_drain.py, fsck.py, purge_bridge.py), so a committed glob tier would escalate the modal class WITHOUT depending on a project token list — directly closing the fitness gap in Finding 1. The existing overlay machinery already supports committed glob triggers (glob_triggered_overlays / applies_to), so this alternative is codebase-aligned and low-blast-radius. The plan should at least judge it and record why token-only committed triggering is at-least-as-good, or adopt a hybrid.
findings.location: Approach section (two-layer lexical trigger design) and Child decomposition (the trigger mechanism child)
scenarios: The modal unlocked-twin class is caught from committed config via a store/lock/drain glob even when a project has authored no trigger_tokens
findings.suggested_fix: Consider adding a small committed `applies_to` glob set (e.g. store/lock/drain/commit source paths) to the concurrency overlay so the modal unlocked-twin class escalates from committed config, because tokens alone miss the repo's stated modal race class (git rm/commit, getmtime+remove on index.lock).
